source_text: 在中国文化中，红色通常象征着好运、长寿和幸福。在春节和其他喜庆场合，红色到处可见。人们把现金 作为礼物送给家人或亲密朋友时，通常放在红信封里。红色在中国流行的另一个原因是人们把它与中国革命 和共产党相联系。然而，红色并不总是代表好运和快乐。因为从前死者的名字常用红色书写，用红墨水书写 中国人名被看成是一种冒犯行为。
reference_translation: In Chinese culture, red usually symbolizes good luck, longevity and happiness. Red can be seen everywhere during the Spring Festival and other festive occasions. When people give cash as gifts to their family members or close friends, they usually put it in red envelopes. Another reason why red is popular in China is that people associate it with the Chinese revolution and the Communist Party. However, red doesn't always represent good luck and happiness. Since the names of the deceased were often written in red in the past, writing Chinese names in red ink is regarded as an offensive act.
